name: Soleá (flamenco "mother of cante")
lineage: Andalusian soleá flamenco palo (song-form), considered the "mother of cante" foundational form from which much of the broader flamenco palo system derives. Characterized by the canonical twelve-beat soleá compás (with accents on beats 3, 6, 8, 10, 12), grave-philosophical lyrical content addressing solitude, the existential condition, and contemplative resignation. Performance: solo cantaor voice with sole flamenco guitar accompaniment, in slower tempo than siguiriya with characteristic falsetas (guitar-instrumental-interludes) between vocal sections. The Triana neighborhood of Seville and the Jerez de la Frontera lineages constitute the canonical regional sub-traditions of soleá. Distinguished from siguiriya by soleá's more contemplative-philosophical (vs anguished-tragic) emotional register.
